subject: Post-demo: prompt outputs PII mapping, TTL, and logging controls — MedSyte pilot
messages:
From: Alice Thompson <alice@medsyte.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: MedSyte Security <security@medsyte.com>
Date: Wed, 3 May 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + data handling questions

Thanks for the demo this morning, Soojin — really helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our security and platform teams around prompt outputs and retention: 

1) Examples of PII that will appear in prompts/outputs: patient name, MRN (medical record number), freeform clinical notes with small ADT snippets. We occasionally send whole patient descriptions (no images).
2) Residency: must remain in US-only (data for pilot cannot leave us regions).
3) Retention: default policy is "no long-term storage" for anything classified as PHI; for logs we can tolerate aggregated telemetry but not raw prompts.

Can you confirm what Redwood stores by default for prompt/response pairs, what can be disabled, and whether we can get a short statement that you won’t persist full prompt outputs for the pilot (we'll need this in the security sign-off)?

— Alice
Alice Thompson
Director, Platform Engineering | MedSyte

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Alice Thompson <alice@medsyte.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 May 2028 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap + data handling questions

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear summary and for looping in security. Short answers up front, then specifics and next steps below.

Short answers:
- By default our hosted API retains: request metadata (timestamps, model id, token counts), and (unless disabled) de-identified request/response artifacts used for monitoring and quality — however for enterprise pilots we can enable a no-persist mode that prevents storing raw prompt/response text.
- Residency: we can pin the pilot to our US data region and ensure inference, logging, and backups do not leave that region.
- Retention: we can set TTLs; for pilot we recommend TTL=0 (ephemeral) for prompt bodies and 30 days for telemetry only.

Detailed breakdown (what we can provide in a short statement for your security team):
- Prompt/Output storage: options are (a) Persist (default) (b) Ephemeral (no storage of full text) — we will configure Ephemeral for the pilot.
- Audit logs: we can provide access logs and hashed-event traces (SHA256 of prompts + salts) rather than full text; these satisfy auditing needs without revealing PHI.
- Derived artifacts: embeddings, search indexes, or model-tuned artifacts are not created for the pilot unless explicitly enabled.
- Backups & snapshots: we will disable snapshotting of prompt-level data for the pilot environment.

Attached is a 1-page summary and a SOC2 extract for your security team to review (redwood-pii-handling-summary.pdf, redwood-soc2-extract.pdf).

Next steps I propose:
1) We produce a 1-paragraph pilot commitment statement you can drop into your vendor assessment (I'll draft).
2) Monica (cc'd) will scope the configuration and share the short config doc and QA checklist.
3) If this looks good, we schedule a short call with your security folks to sign off the pilot config.

I can have the one-paragraph statement to you by tomorrow EOD (PST). Does that timeline work?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0134

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Thompson <alice@medsyte.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 May 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap + data handling questions

Hi Alice — jumping in from the Product/CS side. Quick technical clarifications and pilot configuration options so your security team can evaluate: 

Pilot configuration we recommend for MedSyte (US-only, PHI-safe):
- Region: us-west-2 (we can use any US region you prefer).
- Prompt persistence: disabled (no raw prompt or full response persisted).
- Audit logs: enabled with hashed-event traces only (SHA256 + per-tenant salt) and access metadata (who/when).
- Tokenization traces: disabled by default for pilot.
- Derived artifacts: not generated.

Operational notes:
- TTLs: prompt bodies TTL=0 (deleted immediately post-inference), telemetry (aggregated counters/percentiles) TTL=30d.
- Access controls: RBAC for your team plus mTLS for service-to-service calls.
- Evidence: we can provide a signed pilot commitment doc and scoped SOC2 extract (attached).

If you confirm these items, we will: (a) spin up a pinned US-only environment, (b) create a pilot DPA addendum that explicitly states no-persist on prompts for pilot scope, and (c) provide a short test harness so you can verify that prompt bodies are not present in logs.

Action requested: confirm preferred US region and whether your security team needs the hashed traces retained longer than 30 days for incident investigations.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Alice Thompson <alice@medsyte.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 4 May 2028 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap + data handling questions

Thanks Monica — that's exactly the level of detail we need. A couple of clarifications:

- Please confirm that "deleted immediately post-inference" means no durable persistence in any logging pipeline and that ephemeral caches (KV caches) are also not materialized to disk.
- For hashed-event traces: we need assurance the salt is per-tenant and managed by Redwood (not a predictable global salt).
- For the pilot DPA addendum: we'll want a clause that states Redwood will not materialize prompt/response text and will only retain hashed-event traces for at most 30 days.

Preferred region: us-east-1 (we prefer eastern region for proximity to our infra).

If you can send the 1-paragraph commitment and the DPA addendum draft, I can route them to our procurement and security teams for sign-off. Also, timeline: we aim to start the pilot the week of 5/20 if everything is cleared.

— Alice

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Alice Thompson <alice@medsyte.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 May 2028 17:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap + data handling questions

Alice — thanks, confirmed. Short commitments below (I will also attach a signed one-paragraph statement and route the DPA draft via legal):

Commitments for MedSyte pilot (to include in vendor assessment):
- Residency: all inference, logging, and backups for the pilot will be pinned to us-east-1.
- No-persist: no raw prompt or full response text will be written to persistent storage or backups; ephemeral in-memory KV caches will not be materialized to disk.
- Hashed traces: per-tenant salt; Redwood manages the salt and key lifecycle; hashed-event traces retained for a maximum of 30 days unless otherwise requested in writing.
- Evidence: signed 1-paragraph statement + SOC2 extract attached; DPA addendum draft to follow from Legal within 48 business hours.

Next steps / timeline:
- Today EOD: I’ll upload the signed 1-paragraph commitment and the SOC2 extract to the HubSpot deal and the sharepoint folder (links included).
- Mon (5/8): Legal sends DPA addendum draft for pilot.
- Week of 5/20: stand up pilot environment in us-east-1 and start sample traffic (you’ll have a small test harness to verify no prompt persistence).

If that aligns with your procurement timeline, I’ll proceed and mark the deal stage accordingly.

Thanks again — I’ll follow up with the attachments and links now.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
